evidence.claim: Colored sandstone and abandoned borax mines along a desert byway
evidence.quote: Bitter Springs Back Country Byway offers a drive with many rock formations, like the Muddy Mountains and colorful sandstone for sightseeing. Along the byway, visit abandoned borax mines and evidence of rivers that have long since dried up.

evidence.claim: From Valley of Fire Highway, the unimproved Bitter Spring Trail crosses the northwest of the Muddy Mountains into the northern part of Bitter Spring Valley. It continues through the valley and Bitter Spring Wash toward Echo Bay, on the Overton Arm of Lake Mead.
evidence.quote: An unimproved route from Echo Bay traverses Bitter Spring Wash, Bitter Spring Valley, then the North Section of the valley, and traverses through the northwest of the Muddy Mountains to meet Valley of Fire Highway.

evidence.claim: The agency allows two to four hours for the 28-mile drive.
evidence.quote: Allow 2 to 4 hours to enjoy the 28 miles.

evidence.claim: Echo Bay, on the Overton Arm of Lake Mead.
evidence.quote: The Bitter Spring Wash exits east-northeastwards into the Overton Arm of Lake Mead, at Echo Bay, Nevada.
An unimproved route, named Bitter Spring Trail traverses the Muddy Mountains and the valley

evidence.claim: The Muddy Mountains surround the northern section of Bitter Spring Valley. Coming from Valley of Fire Highway, the unimproved route crosses the northwest of the range before entering the valley. Within the mountains, Congress established the 48,154-acre Muddy Mountains Wilderness in 2002. BLM and the National Park Service manage that wilderness, where elevations range from 1,700 to 5,400 feet.

evidence.claim: Bitter Ridge divides Bitter Spring Valley into two sections. Its four-mile arc separates the longer southern section from a northern basin bordered by the Muddy Mountains to the west, northwest and north. Water from the northern section drains southeast into two washes; the southern washes combine and flow toward Echo Bay. Muddy Peak, at 5,363 feet, borders the valley directly to the west, adjacent to Bitter Ridge but not connected to it.
evidence.quote: The arc shaped 4 mi (6.4 km) long Bitter Ridge separates the longer South Section from a North Section surrounded by the Muddy Mountains west, northwest, and north. The North Section drains southeastwards into two washes that meet the South Section. The washes in the South Section combine to flow east-northeast to Echo Bay, Overton Arm.

evidence.claim: At Echo Bay, Bitter Spring Wash reaches the Overton Arm of Lake Mead. The valley lies on the lake’s western edge, between bordering mountain ranges. North Shore Road provides the major southern approach to Echo Bay and the eastern valley, crossing the northeastern sections of the Black Mountains. The wash, valley and mountain crossing described here belong to the unimproved route that connects Echo Bay with Valley of Fire Highway.
